newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila to cut forward forex cover for oil firms.
newsitem.headline: Manila to cut forward forex cover for oil firms.

text.p: Finance Secretary Roberto De Ocampo said on Thursday the forward foreign exchange cover offered to oil importers would be reduced to 60 days from 90 beginning on January 1 next year and abolished by March.
It will be cut by 30 days each in the following months, completely abolishing it by March 1, 1997 in preparation for full deregulation of the local oil industry.

The original schedule for cutting back on the forward cover was to begin on December 1, 1996 but it was deferred upon a request by Manila's three oil firms, Pilipinas Shell Petroleum Corp, a unit of Royal Shell Group Caltex (Philippines) Inc and Petron Corp.
The firms had sought the deferment on grounds the government still owed them money from an oil buffer fund.
The forward foreign exchange cover meant that the country's central bank took the risk of fluctuations in the peso-dollar exchange rate on behalf of the oil importers.
